content: Photosensitivity refers to the degree to which an object or substance reacts when exposed to photons of light. In the context of medicine, photosensitivity describes a condition in which individuals experience discomfort or are prone to sunburn when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) light. This UV light may originate from natural sunlight or artificial sources such as tanning beds. The condition is often triggered by an allergic reaction or as a side effect of certain medications. In the field of electronic engineering, photosensitivity pertains to the design and function of specific electronic devices, such as photodiodes and charge-coupled devices (CCDs), which are engineered to respond to light. These devices utilize the photoelectric effect, a phenomenon where electrons are emitted from a material upon the absorption of electromagnetic radiation. When light strikes the active surface of these devices, the electrical current flowing through them or the electrical charge stored within them changes in proportion to the light's intensity and wavelength. This property enables these devices to perform various sensing and regulatory functions. For instance, a photoresistor circuit can detect ambient light levels to activate a street lamp at dusk. Similarly, digital cameras employ CCDs with high sensitivity to light, allowing them to convert incoming photons into precise electrical charges. These charges are then encoded into binary files, which can be stored and later displayed on digital screens or other media. In chemistry, photosensitivity describes the tendency of certain chemicals to undergo reactions when exposed to light. Substances such as hydrogen peroxide and many prescription drugs are photosensitive and are therefore stored in tinted or opaque containers to prevent photodegradation. Photosensitive devices include the human retina and photographic film. Photographic film is photosensitive because its material undergoes a chemical reaction when exposed to light. Common photosensitive substances include alkali salts and silver halides. Photosensitivity can also occur as a side effect of certain medications. Drugs known to cause photosensitivity include, but are not limited to, the following: Alitretinoin Atovaquone and proguanil hydrochloride Bexarotene Chlorpropamide Clemastine Demeclocycline hydrochloride Dibucaine Doxycycline Doxorubicin Hydrochloride Epirubicin Fosaprepitant Hexachlorophene Hydrochlorothiazide Ciprofloxacin Cidofovir Cromolyn Flucytosine Lomefloxacin hydrochloride Methotrexate Olsalazine Oxaprozin Oxytetracycline Perphenazine Tiagabine Tolbutamide Tolazamide Vandetanib
